title: Executable quality rule catalog
description: The catalog that gives every approved rule of the product an identity, a risk class and the evidence it demands. The loader that judges it is tools/qualitycatalog, and a test holds this document and that loader together: a rule this schema calls invalid must be refused by the loader, and the two must not drift into two different contracts.

schema_version.description: The only catalog version the loader understands. A judge and a document that disagree about the version must not silently agree about the rules.

rules.description: The rules of the product. An empty catalog verifies nothing, so it is refused rather than accepted as vacuously true.

id.description: Stable identity of the rule. Never reused and never renumbered: the id is what a waiver, an inventory row and a review are keyed by, so a gap in the sequence is harmless and a duplicate is not.

source.description: The versioned document the rule comes from, relative to the repository root, optionally followed by an #anchor.

description.description: The rule in one sentence, in the product's vocabulary.

risk.description: The risk class of the quality program: Q0 critical, Q1 high, Q2 normal. The class decides which evidence the loader demands.

modules.description: The packages that own the rule. Each one must be a directory of the checkout.

actors.description: The actors the rule speaks about (visitor, account, moderator, provider).

states.description: The states of the entity the rule speaks about.

authorization.description: Who is allowed to do this, and what the refusal looks like. Required as a non-empty statement for every rule and as a test for Q0.

concurrency.description: What two simultaneous requests do. Required as a non-empty statement for every rule and as a test for Q0.

idempotency.description: What a replay does. Required as a non-empty statement for every rule and as a test for Q0.

security.description: The security property the rule protects. Never optional: a rule whose security meaning is unstated is a rule nobody can review.

privacy.description: The personal data the rule touches and how it is minimized. Never optional, for the same reason as security.

evidence.description: Documents that state the rule; each path must exist in the checkout.

not_applicable.description: A written reason for each evidence category that has no test. Declaring a reason for a category that already has tests is a contradiction, and an empty reason is not a decision.

tests.description: The evidence slots of a rule. Positive and negative are demanded of every rule; the remaining slots are demanded by risk class, and a slot a rule cannot fill needs a written reason in not_applicable.

items.description: `path::Function`, relative to the repository root. The checkout must hold that file and the file must declare that name; a reference nobody can open is a claim about nothing.
